verses.text: Then I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow above his head. His face was like the sun, and his legs were like pillars of fire.

xrefs.text: The appearance of the brilliant light all around Him was like that of a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell facedown and heard a voice speaking.
There He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as the light.
His feet were like polished bronze refined in a furnace, and His voice was like the roar of many waters.
And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming in a loud voice, “Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?
His body was like beryl, his face like the brilliance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of polished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude.
The One seated there looked like jasper and carnelian, and a rainbow that gleamed like an emerald encircled the throne.
Then the sixth angel sounded his trumpet, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar before God

And as I observed, I heard an eagle flying overhead, calling in a loud voice, “Woe! Woe! Woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the trumpet blasts about to be sounded by the remaining three angels!

notes.note: If your language does not use this passive form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [whose clothing was a cloud]

John speaks of the angel as if he were wearing a cloud as his clothing. This expression could be understood as figurative. However, because very unusual things were often seen in visions, it could also be understood as a literally true statement in its context. Alternate translation: [in the midst of a cloud]

notes.quote: καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς στῦλοι πυρός
notes.note: The point of these comparisons is that the angel’s face was very bright, like the sun, and that the angel’s feet were glowing like fire. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make these points explicitly. It may be helpful to begin a new sentence here. Alternate translation: [The angel’s face was very bright, like the sun, and his feet were glowing as if they were on fire]

Since John compares the feet of the angel to pillars, it is likely that by feet he means “legs” by association. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his legs]

verses.text: He held in his hand a small scroll, which lay open. He placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land.

xrefs.text: Then the angel I had seen standing on the sea and on the land lifted up his right hand to heaven.
Then I looked and saw a hand reaching out to me, and in it was a scroll,
Then the voice that I had heard from heaven spoke to me again, saying, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.
Then I saw a scroll in the right hand of the One seated on the throne. It had writing on both sides and was sealed with seven seals.
Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.
Ask Me, and I will make the nations Your inheritance, the ends of the earth Your possession.
With awesome deeds of righteousness You answer us, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas.
And when the Lamb opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, “Come!

notes.note: If your language does not use this passive form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [a little scroll that he had opened]

John is using the adjective left as a noun to mean a certain one of the angel’s feet. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you could translate this word with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and his left foot]

verses.text: Then he cried out in a loud voice like the roar of a lion. And when he cried out, the seven thunders sounded their voices.

xrefs.text: For this is what the LORD has said to me: “Like a lion roaring or a young lion over its prey— and though a band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their shouting or subdued by their clamor — so the LORD of Hosts will come down to do battle on Mount Zion and its heights.
He said: “The LORD roars from Zion and raises His voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers.”
The LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will tremble. But the LORD will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.
From the throne came flashes of lightning, rumblings, and peals of thunder. Before the throne burned seven torches of fire. These are the seven spirits of God.
The LORD goes forth like a mighty one; He stirs up His zeal like a warrior. He shouts; yes, He roars in triumph over His enemies:

So you are to prophesy all these words against them and say to them: ‘The LORD will roar from on high; He will raise His voice from His holy habitation. He will roar loudly over His pasture; like those who tread the grapes, He will call out with a shout against all the inhabitants of the earth.
And I heard a sound from heaven like the roar of many waters and the loud rumbling of thunder. And the sound I heard was like harpists strumming their harps.
The lion has roared— who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken— who will not prophesy?

notes.note: The point of this comparison is probably that the loud voice of the angel commanded attention like the roar of a lion. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [in a loud voice that commanded attention as does a lion’s roar]

John speaks of these seven thunders as if he assumes that his readers will know what or who they are, but he has not introduced or explained them earlier in the book and interpreters are not certain of their identity. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could introduce them in such a way as to indicate that John has not identified them previously. Alternate translation: [seven thunders spoke]

This expression could mean that thunder spoke or sounded seven times, rather than that seven different thunders spoke. You could say that in your translation or indicate this possibility in a footnote. Alternate translation: [thunder spoke seven times] or [thunder sounded seven times]
It might seem that the expression spoke their own voices contains extra information that would be unnatural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [spoke]

verses.text: When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to put it in writing. But I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down.

xrefs.text: But you, Daniel, shut up these words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will roam to and fro, and knowledge will increase.”
The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been spoken is true. Now you must seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future.”
“Go on your way, Daniel,” he replied, “for the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end.
The secret things belong to the LORD our God, but the things revealed belong to us and to our children forever, so that we may follow all the words of this law.
Then he told me, “Do not seal up the words of prophecy in this book, because the time is near.
Then the LORD answered me: “Write down this vision and clearly inscribe it on tablets, so that a herald may run with it.
Bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples.
saying, “Write on a scroll what you see and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.

notes.note: The implication is that John was going to write down what the seven thunders had said. You can provide this information in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I was going to write down what they had said]

notes.quote: σφράγισον ἃ ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, καὶ μὴ αὐτὰ γράψῃς
notes.note: The voice spoke as if John should literally seal what the thunders said. However, since the voice then specified that John was not to write anything down, the voice meant that John should keep secret what the thunders said. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Keep secret what the seven thunders said by not writing it down]

verses.text: Then the angel I had seen standing on the sea and on the land lifted up his right hand to heaven.

xrefs.text: And the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven, and I heard him swear by Him who lives forever, saying, “It will be for a time, and times, and half a time. When the power of the holy people has finally been shattered, all these things will be completed.”
For I lift up My hand to heaven and declare: As surely as I live forever,
Then the seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came from the throne in the temple, saying, “It is done!
“Worthy are You, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for You created all things; by Your will they exist and were created.
And he said in a loud voice, “Fear God and give Him glory, because the hour of His judgment has come. Worship the One who made the heavens and the earth and the sea and the springs of waters.

“Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.
He held in his hand a small scroll, which lay open. He placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land.
the Living One. I was dead, and behold, now I am alive forever and ever! And I hold the keys of Death and of Hades.

notes.quote: ἦρεν τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ τὴν δεξιὰν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν
notes.note: The angel raised his right hand to heaven as a symbolic action to show that he was swearing an oath by God. If this would not be clear to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action. Alternate translation: [raised his right hand to heaven to show that he swearing an oath by God]

verses.text: And he swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it: “There will be no more delay!

xrefs.text: “Worthy are You, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for You created all things; by Your will they exist and were created.
Then the seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came from the throne in the temple, saying, “It is done!
And whenever the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to the One seated on the throne, who lives forever and ever,

notes.quote: τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων
notes.note: John assumes that his readers will understand that the angel is referring to God with this expression. You can indicate that explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [by the eternal God]
This expression refers to endless future time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for all eternity]

notes.quote: τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ
notes.note: The angel is using the three parts of creation to mean all of creation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the entire creation]
In this context, the word time means a delay. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [no further delay]

verses.text: But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he begins to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be fulfilled, just as He proclaimed to His servants the prophets.

xrefs.text: that is, the mystery made known to me by revelation, as I have already written briefly.
Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery concealed for ages past
Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.
Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His plan to His servants the prophets.
Heaven must take Him in until the time comes for the restoration of all things, which God announced long ago through His holy prophets.
I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers, so that you will not be conceited: A hardening in part has come to Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.
Then the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and loud voices called out in heaven: “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever.

notes.quote: ἀλλ’ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ ἑβδόμου ἀγγέλου, ὅταν μέλλῃ σαλπίζειν
notes.note: These two phrases mean similar things. The angel is using repetition to emphasize the idea that the phrases express. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them. Alternate translation: [but in the days when the seventh angel is going to sound a trumpet]

This possessive form does not describe what the seventh angel sounds like. Instead, it describes a sound that the seventh angel will make. Alternate translation: [when the seventh angel makes a sound]

The angel is using the term days idiomatically to refer to a specific time. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at the time of the sound]
If your language does not use this passive form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [God will accomplish his mystery]

verses.text: Then the voice that I had heard from heaven spoke to me again, saying, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.

xrefs.text: When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to put it in writing. But I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down.
He held in his hand a small scroll, which lay open. He placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land.
And whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear this command behind you: “This is the way. Walk in it.”

notes.quote: τὸ βιβλίον τὸ ἠνεῳγμένον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ τοῦ ἀγγέλου, τοῦ ἑστῶτος ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
notes.note: If your language does not use this passive form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the scroll that the angel standing on the sea and on the land has opened and is holding in his hand]

verses.text: And I went to the angel and said, “Give me the small scroll. “Take it and eat it, he said. “It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.”

xrefs.text: “Son of man,” He said to me, “eat what you find here. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.”
Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words became my joy and my heart’s delight. For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts.
And you, son of man, listen to what I tell you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I give you.”
I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my daily bread.
So the Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness and in the anger of my spirit, with the strong hand of the LORD upon me.
Because of these, the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience.

verses.text: So I took the small scroll from the angel’s hand and ate it, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth. But when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.

xrefs.text: “Son of man,” He said to me, “eat and fill your stomach with this scroll I am giving you.” So I ate, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.
How sweet are Your words to my taste— sweeter than honey in my mouth!
Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
They are more precious than gold, than much pure gold; they are sweeter than honey, than honey from the comb.
May my meditation be pleasing to Him, for I rejoice in the LORD.
So the Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness and in the anger of my spirit, with the strong hand of the LORD upon me.
which He unrolled before me. And written on the front and back of it were words of lamentation, mourning, and woe.

notes.note: If your language does not use this passive form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [it made my stomach bitter]

verses.text: And they told me, “You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and tongues and kings.

xrefs.text: And He said to me, “Prophesy concerning these bones and tell them, ‘Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD!
Then the LORD reached out His hand, touched my mouth, and said to me: “Behold, I have put My words in your mouth.

Then He said to me, “Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and tell the breath that this is what the Lord GOD says: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live!”
For three and a half days all peoples and tribes and tongues and nations will view their bodies and will not permit them to be laid in a tomb.
Then I saw another angel flying overhead, with the eternal gospel to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth— to every nation and tribe and tongue and people.
Then the angel said to me, “The waters you saw, where the prostitute was seated, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: “Take from My hand this cup of the wine of wrath, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink from it.

notes.note: The pronoun they is an indefinite pronoun that does not have a specific referent in the immediate context. John is using this indefinite construction to focus on what he was told rather than on who told it to him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this with a different expression that does not use an indefinite pronoun. Alternate translation: [I was told]

notes.quote: λαοῖς, καὶ ἔθνεσιν, καὶ γλώσσαις, καὶ βασιλεῦσιν πολλοῖς
notes.note: In this context, the terms peoples, nations, languages, and kings mean similar things. John is using the four terms together to make a comprehensive statement. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [every different people group]

notes.quote: λαοῖς, καὶ ἔθνεσιν, καὶ γλώσσαις, καὶ βασιλεῦσιν πολλοῖς
notes.note: The angel is referring to speakers of various languages by association with the languages themselves, and John is referring to the subjects of various kingdoms by association with their kings. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [many peoples and nations and speakers of many languages and subjects of many kingdoms]

named.name: Gentile
named.brief: A non-Jewish person; someone from the nations
